question: Which of the following has NOT occurred after the liberalisation of economic policies under the New Economic Policies (NEP) in 1991?

options.text: Increase in India’s share of exports in world trade
Significant increase in India’s foreign exchange reserves
Increase in inflows from foreign direct investment
A massive increase in the share of agriculture in India’s gross domestic product

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: A massive increase in the share of agriculture in India's gross domestic product**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• After the liberalisation of economic policies under the New Economic Policies (NEP) in 1991, there was no massive increase in the share of agriculture in India's GDP.

• In fact, the share of agriculture in GDP has been declining over the years due to rapid growth in the industrial and services sectors.

• The NEP aimed at reducing the role of the public sector in the economy and encouraging private sector participation, which led to significant growth in industrial and services sectors rather than agriculture.

• Agriculture's share in GDP has been decreasing from about 30% in the early 1990s to around 15-20% in recent years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **New Economic Policy (NEP) 1991**

• The NEP 1991 was a set of economic reforms introduced to liberalize and globalize the Indian economy.

• **Increase in India's share of exports in world trade**

• Post-1991, India's share in global trade has increased due to liberalization policies that reduced trade barriers and promoted exports.

• India's exports have diversified and increased in both goods and services sectors.

• **Significant increase in India's foreign exchange reserves**

• One of the most notable outcomes of the NEP was the substantial increase in foreign exchange reserves.

• From a precarious level in 1991, reserves have grown significantly, providing a cushion against external economic shocks.

• **Increase in inflows from foreign direct investment (FDI)**

• The NEP 1991 led to a significant increase in FDI inflows as restrictions on foreign investment were eased and foreign investors were given more incentives to invest in India.

• FDI has played a crucial role in the development of various sectors, including manufacturing, infrastructure, and services.

• **Share of Agriculture in GDP**

• The share of agriculture in India's GDP has been on a declining trend, reflecting the structural transformation of the economy.

• As the economy develops, the contribution of agriculture typically decreases while the industrial and services sectors grow.

• This trend is consistent with global patterns observed in other developing and developed economies.
